dugout: A dugout is not assembled, so there is no keel and nothing is measured from one. The work starts with a standing tree, not a timber on blocks.
The hull is chosen, not designed. Its beam is the trunk's beam and cannot exceed it, which fixes what the boat can ever be before a tool touches it.
Burned and adzed out from above. There is no seam anywhere in the hull, so nothing can leak — and nothing can be replaced either, because there are no parts.
The gunwale is dressed to a fair curve and left thick, because the rim takes the paddle strokes and every landing. Below it the hull is already complete: there is nothing left to add.
